documents.title: Potential impact of AI on our academic mission
documents.summary: A 2023 provost letter that sets no university AI rule: instructors decide whether and how far students may use AI and must state this clearly, unapproved use falls under the Academic Code, and the letter points to resources on citation, data protection, research use and IP.
documents.stance_why: The letter says 'While the University is not prescribing specific AI policies' and that 'instructors may choose whether or not to allow the use of AI tools and to what extent', so it sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors: delegates.

units.policy: instructors may choose whether or not to allow the use of AI tools and to what extent

units.policy: faculty should offer clear, unambiguous information about what is, and is not, allowed in their courses

documents.title: GAITL report and next steps for GenAI
documents.summary: A July 2026 provost memo summarizing the GAITL committee report. It sets no rule but endorses university baseline rules with departmental and faculty autonomy, enterprise AI tools, faculty training and academic-code updates, and calls the plan a living document.
documents.stance_why: The memo recommends 'university-wide baseline policies' while 'preserving departmental and faculty autonomy to set localized standards', and says templates are still to be drafted; it imposes no stance itself and hands decisions to faculty and departments: delegates.

units.why: The memo reports the committee's recommendation that 'Brown should establish university-wide baseline policies for GenAI use' to give a common understanding of acceptable use; an institution-wide framework, P56. It is a recommendation, so modality should.
units.anchor: Brown should establish university-wide baseline policies for GenAI use

units.why: Alongside the baseline, the committee stresses 'preserving departmental and faculty autonomy to set localized standards', so rules are set locally; P04.
units.anchor: preserving departmental and faculty autonomy to set localized standards for their specific courses

units.why: The recommendation is to expand 'secure, enterprise-level AI tools' via OIT for privacy and equitable access, i.e. a sanctioned university-provided tool (P17); P50/P51 are the stated reasons but the rule itself is providing tools.

units.why: Sheridan and the Library should 'develop and administer additional specialized training to support faculty and staff AI literacy', i.e. support for faculty learning AI; P63.
units.anchor: develop and administer additional specialized training to support faculty and staff AI literacy

units.why: Updating the academic codes 'to explicitly address boundaries of AI assistance' concerns which AI help counts as misconduct under integrity processes; P36 is the nearest type.

units.policy: formally update the College and Graduate School academic codes to explicitly address boundaries of AI assistance

units.policy: Build or join a coalition of peer universities to set shared national standards for AI in teaching and learning.
units.uncovered_note: Build or join a coalition of peer universities to set shared national standards for AI in teaching and learning.

documents.unit: Generative AI in Teaching and Learning Committee
documents.title: GAITL Committee Final Report
documents.summary: The 2026 final report of Brown's Generative AI in Teaching and Learning committee. It reports survey and syllabus evidence, sets ten guiding principles and six phased recommendations (university baseline rules with departmental and instructor autonomy, enterprise tools, training, academic-code updates), and lists existing supports and course examples. It is a set of recommendations, not binding policy.
documents.stance_why: The report recommends 'university-wide baseline rules for GenAI while departments/programs develop and publish standards' and says instructors' 'professional judgment ... should supersede University baseline rules'; it sets no binding stance and leaves decisions to instructors: delegates.

units.policy: a reconstituted and expanded GAITL Committee will work this summer to draft a range of AI policy templates

units.anchor: whether the committee should steer the University toward an institution-wide baseline policy for AI use

units.policy: focusing on the pursuit of knowledge, academic freedom and free inquiry, and the centering of disciplinary expertise

notes: Brown has no school-level or computing-department AI policy found; course pages deferred. All four documents are university-layer. The Sheridan page's five sample syllabus statements are from non-CS courses (HMAN, CSCI 2200 cybersecurity law, ENGN, LANG, DSIO) and are coded as exemplar text offered to instructors, not binding rules. The GAITL report is a recommendations document, so many units have modality should or informs. Uncovered units: coalition for national standards, AI literacy course designation, committee disclosure of own AI use, students co-designing rules, explaining reasons for AI rules, de-emphasizing punishment, staff declining to debug LLM code.
